labelling: Labels are INHERITED from the URL dataset (weak labelling). A page is labelled phishing because its URL was, not because the page content was independently reviewed.
known_biases: Taken-down phishing URLs often serve parking or error pages; recognisable ones are dropped, the rest is label noise.
Benign URLs that have gone dead are lost, biasing the benign side toward sites still online.
Retrieval rate differs by class, so the surviving sample is not a random sample of either class.
Pages are parsed statically; JavaScript-rendered content is invisible to these features.
safety: GET only; no form submitted and no credential ever sent.
No JavaScript executed; HTML parsed as a static document.
SSRF-guarded: private, loopback, link-local, multicast and reserved addresses refused, re-checked on every redirect.
Capped at 800,000 bytes and 5 redirects per page.
